notes:
Summary: Lost to TogetherAI after prolonged procurement. Primary reasons: competitor offered bundled on-prem appliance + licensing, lower short-term TCO, and an existing technical partnership with their cloud vendor.

Timeline (bullets):
- 2024-09-12: Intro call (AE Maya) - discussed clinical-chat assistant + PHI handling. Customer: integration with Epic via middleware.
- 2024-09-26: Security review intake submitted (shared SOC2 + architecture). Rafael onsite demo planned.
- 2024-10-10: Demo (Rafael) - showed dedicated GPU perf numbers for 4k token context; client requested latency targets: <150ms p50 for short prompts, burst 400 qps for triage flows.
- 2024-10-24: POC kickoff - supplied test corpus (de-id transcripts), ran hosted POC for 2 weeks. Fireflies id ff_2024-11-06_1432_lhca-poc-call (POC sync).
- 2024-11-15: POC results: Redwood dedicated met quality targets but costs higher than Together quote (especially factoring on-prem appliance amortization). Latency fine; throughput with caching/continuous batching acceptable.
- 2024-12-02: Security: customer asked for HSM/KMS integration and stricter retention controls. They required an on-prem option with air-gapped ingest for certain PHI subsets.
- 2024-12-18: Procurement request - Lighthouse exec team put hiring freeze/budget hold across AI projects til Q2.
- 2025-01-08: Customer informs Redwood they selected TogetherAI (better licensing for appliance and existing partner discounts).
- 2025-01-18: Final wrap call; documented lessons and closed as loss.

Key technical notes / quotes:
- "We liked Redwood's runtime — quality was good — but Together had a turnkey appliance and a cheaper multi-year amortization model."
- Team was explicit about needing an on-premizable appliance for PHI-heavy triage. Redwood offered Private + on-prem packaging but procurement prioritized vendor with existing appliance commitments.
- Security team: wanted SOC2 + on-prem HSM + per-request audit log export. Redwood answered audit + KMS, but customer's timeline to certify vendor was shorter and Together's compliance paperwork was already in place.

Why we lost (short):
- Price/contract structure (Together offered CAPEX appliance + discount, lower initial outlay).
- Security/compliance fit: existing partner relationship and faster vendor cert path for Together.
- No internal champion after budget freeze — clinical sponsor reallocated.
- Procurement timeline accelerated to Q1 and they chose vendor already in their cloud ecosystem.

Open follow-ups and internal notes:
- Mark account for 6-mo re-engage (target 2025-07) — watch policy changes and budget cycles.
- Save POC perf artifacts: latency/throughput graphs in drive link. Rafael to prepare short win/loss doc for product team: detail appliance vs private deployment gaps.
- Consider building appliance-compatible offer sheet or financing term to compete on CAPEX-heavy procurement deals.
